title: Routes are cached by merge SHA and read from fact cards
acceptance: The router is shown each pull request through a pure context contract read from its fact card (number, title, labels, areas with diff stats, flags, the first 600 characters of the body, quoted with < escaped); a test pins its fields and its byte size on the recorded week, and the before and after bytes are written in docs/plans/RISE-CHANGES.md.

Each admitted route is written as cache/routes/<mergeSha>.json { schema, mergeSha, route, contract, at }, contract the sha256 of the router's system text, the route context version and FACTS_VERSION; a cached route is used only when the file admits strictly under the current contract and menu, and a malformed or mismatched file is ignored and routed afresh.
A pull request whose answer could not be read is asked once more; still unread it stays unrouted and is not cached; the run log counts router calls, the retry among them, and routes from the cache.

A re-run over the same period with the same cache makes zero router calls, and a superseding run routes every pull request the first digest routed exactly as before (the #685 and #693 case of 2026-10-16-2).

Both Changes workflows check changes-data out read-only without credentials before the run, pass it as --cache, and commit only the new route files beside the digest on non-dry runs; the published digest format is unchanged.

activity.summary: Opened and claimed as P1-C of the RISE Changes v2 Phase 1 plan (owner-approved 2026-11-06).

summary: The router reads fact-card summaries through a pinned context contract, each route is cached on changes-data by merge SHA under a contract hash, and an unreadable answer is asked for once more, so re-runs and supersedes route as the first run did.
